evidence: The original wire.ts comment said 'every click URL is dispatch?e=…' while parseHandlerUrl still accepts direct cc-candybar://<verb>/… URLs; 39d887b narrowed it to 'every URL effectsUrl emits'.
guidance_note: When a header comment states a universal invariant ('every X is Y'), check it against the accepted-input side as well as the emit side before committing.

evidence: The original test declared `const dirs: string[] = []` but writeTranscript never pushed into it, so afterAll removed nothing. The flag is a false positive: 39d887b only edited a comment in src/click/wire.ts, and the leaking cleanup was in the original test.
guidance_note: When a test creates temp resources, assert that cleanup actually runs (e.g. count leftover cc-cache-* dirs) instead of trusting the afterAll loop.

evidence: The original oneArg returned `decodeSegments(value)[0]`, which cuts a direct `copy/a/b` down to 'a'. The flag is a false positive: 86e97fa only touched test/segment-cache.test.ts.
guidance_note: When moving value decoding from the URL parser into per-verb handlers, test each verb with the legacy direct-URL shapes it used to accept (slash-bearing values included) before pushing.

evidence: The original `rest.search(/[/?]/)` treated `?` as a verb delimiter, which broke bare `hello?world`. The reviewer proposed making `?` verb-conditional; the agent instead moved dispatch to `dispatch/e=…` so `/` is the only delimiter, which is a cleaner fix. The flag is a false positive: 86e97fa was test-only.
guidance_note: When adding a new delimiter to an existing URL grammar, list the documented legacy forms (bare copy) and check that none of them contains the new delimiter as data.

evidence: The original cache.ts imported openSync/readSync/statSync and read synchronously on the render path, bypassing the gated transcript-fs seam. 88d18e3 added a gated readTail and made cacheExpiresAt async. The flag is a false positive: 86e97fa was test-only.
guidance_note: Before writing a new transcript reader, grep for the repo's existing gated I/O seam (transcript-fs) and route through it from the first commit.

evidence: The fact is true: cacheTimer is absent from DEFAULT_DSL_CONFIG.layout, so it never renders by default. The agent's point that block/weekly are also defined but not in the default layout is consistent with the hunk. The packet does not show whether the 'restore' in the PR title meant the timer used to render by default, so the product call can't be settled. The flag is a false positive: 88d18e3 did not touch default-dsl-config.ts.
guidance_note: When a PR title says 'restore' a visible feature but the feature ships opt-in, say so in the PR body or next to the segment, so a reviewer doesn't read it as a wiring gap.

evidence: F3's fix changed the daemon's single-arg verbs to decode the whole value, but test/helpers/click.ts effectsOf still ran decodeSegments for every verb, so it no longer mirrored the daemon. The agent said so itself: 'the helper could have masked the very regression the prior fix repaired'. 13e204c added decodeArgs.
guidance_note: When changing a decode contract, grep for every mirror of it, test helpers included (decodeSegments callers), and update them in the same commit.

evidence: F4's fix moved the wire from `dispatch?e=` to `dispatch/e=`, but the test helper header still said `dispatch?e=…`; 13e204c rewrote the comment.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a wire literal, grep the repo for the old literal (`dispatch?e`) in comments and helpers before pushing.

evidence: The reviewer's mechanism ('an escaped snippet such as "cache_read_input_tokens":1 in message content will still satisfy this regex') is wrong: in JSONL, quotes inside a content string serialize as \", and CACHE_HIT_RE needs `tokens":` with no backslash before the closing quote. The agent's regression decoy is built with JSON.stringify, so it would pass against the old code too, which makes the test vacuous. Hardening against unescaped nested objects is defensible, but the packet doesn't show that such lines exist. The flag is a false positive: 13e204c was test-only, and the scan logic predates review.
guidance_note: Before accepting a false-positive claim, run the regression test against the unfixed code and confirm it fails; a decoy that passes both ways proves nothing.

evidence: The original dispatch wrapped every collected error in `throw new BadVerbArgs(...)`, turning operational failures into BAD_REQUEST against the dispatcher's input/operational split. The flag is a false positive: cb623b3 only touched cache.ts and its test.
guidance_note: When an aggregator folds errors from leaf handlers, keep each error's class through the fold, so the aggregate is classified the way the leaves were.

evidence: readTail was written in 88d18e3 as F5's fix and made one `fh.read(buf, 0, buf.length, start)` call with no short-read loop. The single-read shape was carried over from the old readSync code. 338cb9d added the fill loop.
guidance_note: When writing a new positional-read helper, use the read-until-filled-or-EOF loop from the start rather than porting a single read call.

evidence: The original PR added showOperation/showTimeSinceCommit to gitOptionsFromClosure's return value but not to its hand-written return type. Instead of patching that literal type, 7d3ee7c extracted one GitInfoOptions interface. The flag is a false positive: 338cb9d only touched transcript-fs.ts.
guidance_note: When adding a field to one copy of a hand-duplicated option shape, grep for the other copies and extract a shared type instead of editing one of them.

evidence: The set-state comment said a slash-bearing key or value 'round-trips intact', but the reviewer cites the loader and state validators, which reject slash-bearing keys; the agent narrowed it to a codec-only claim. The flag is a false positive: 7d3ee7c only touched git option types. The packet does not show whether that comment was written during review.
guidance_note: When a comment claims end-to-end support, trace the claim through the upstream validators before writing it.

narrative: This was a large PR, and Copilot fed back pre-existing issues about one at a time over nine rounds. Three findings came from incomplete fixes: the decode change missed the test helper (F7), the wire change left a stale comment (F8), and the new readTail shipped without a short-read loop (F11). Each of those rounds also carried an original finding, so no round was purely avoidable. F9 was accepted on a mechanism that JSON escaping defeats, and its regression test is vacuous.
guidance_observations: Fix commits should grep for every mirror of a changed contract (helpers, comments, literals) before pushing. Two of the three fix-caused findings were exactly that kind of miss.
The agent wrote a regression test for F9 without confirming it fails on the old code, so a passing test was taken as proof.

evidence: The removed code already did `percentages.percentage = Math.round(nativePct)`, so rounding native values is pre-existing behavior. Both arms of the new code round, which keeps the field an integer whichever source fills it. The reviewer's request is a preference, not a defect.

This is the same finding as cc-candybar#60/F6, raised again: it's true that cacheTimer is unreachable from the default layout, but whether it should ship in the default is a product choice the packet can't settle. The cited laws decide nothing about default-layout curation.
guidance_note: When pushing back on a design-choice finding, record the decision durably (a comment at the segment declaration) so the next review doesn't raise it again.

evidence: setState calls `decodeSegments(rawValue)`, which can throw a raw URIError on a malformed escape before any BadVerbArgs check runs, so bad input is classified as an operational failure. a157eeb routed it through decodeWire.
guidance_note: When moving decoding to the verb boundary, wrap every decode in the input-error class at that same moment, covering both codecs.

evidence: oneArg is a bare `decodeURIComponent(value)`, which throws URIError on a lone `%`. The dispatcher maps a non-BadVerbArgs error to RENDER_FAILED. The decode came from cc-candybar#60/F3's fix, but the earlier decodeSegments version threw the same way, so this is not fix-caused.
guidance_note: When adding a decode step at an input boundary, add a malformed-input test that asserts the error class.

narrative: Two real classification bugs (raw URIError escaping as RENDER_FAILED) were fixed in one commit with a single decodeWire boundary. Two pushbacks: the rounding one holds, since rounding was pre-existing. The cache-timer default-layout one repeats #60/F6, and the packet can't settle it. The second round was clean.
guidance_observations: The cacheTimer pushback was given twice across PRs; a durable in-code note would have stopped it from being raised again.

evidence: The original renderer ran applySegmentLayout per segment and only then called splitCellsIntoLines, so a width:5 'ABCDE\nFGHIJ' was measured as one cell. 89c0341 splits first and adds a regression test.
guidance_note: When introducing a 'never measure across \n' contract, list every cellLength consumer upstream of the split and add a fixed-width test with an authored newline.

evidence: checkTemplateRefs derives the line via `findKeyLine(ctx.source, declPath.split('.'))`, which can never resolve 'layout when'. 89c0341 passed layoutLine explicitly but kept the path literal 'layout.when'.
guidance_note: When a diagnostic path is synthetic, decide in the same edit both the line and the label the user should see, for each authoring surface.

evidence: 89c0341 fixed the line for node `when` errors but left the path hard-coded as 'layout.when' (and the segment-entry path as 'layout'), even though the code already probed for `root`. 9e9fc30 made the path follow the authored surface.
guidance_note: When fixing one field of a diagnostic (line), check its sibling fields (path, message) against every authoring surface the code distinguishes.

evidence: The original renderer already emitted multiple lines per leaf (`splitCellsIntoLines(cells).flatMap(...)`), while dsl-types said a cells leaf renders to ONE strip. The flag is a false positive: 9e9fc30 touched only the loader and its tests, and the stale doc dates from the original PR.
guidance_note: When a PR changes a type's runtime contract, grep that type's doc comments for the old cardinality word ('ONE strip') and fix every occurrence.

evidence: The reviewer cites protocol.ts:18-21, which says renaming wire fields requires a PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. The agent's counter-claims ('the Rust client never touches it', 'developer introspection surface, not the versioned render wire') cannot be checked from the packet. The flag is a false positive: ec787d2 only edited a doc comment, and the root rename is original.
guidance_note: When pushing back against a documented contract, quote the contract's scope from the code rather than asserting which consumers exist.

evidence: 9e9fc30 made `findKeyLine(ctx.source, ['root'])` the path discriminator, so a layout-authored config with `variables: { root: ... }` now reports path 'root' where it previously reported 'layout'. adf6330 switched to parsing the top-level keys.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a discriminator, check it against inputs that share the key name at other depths, and prefer a structural read over a text search from the start.

evidence: authoredLayoutKey (adf6330) needs the source text, but the daemon's validateConfig call never passed source, so production root-authored configs fall back to 'layout'. The gap dates from F3's source-dependent discriminator. The agent confirmed it and threaded source through loadConfig.
guidance_note: When a fix depends on an input (ctx.source), trace every production caller to confirm it supplies that input, not just the test helpers.

evidence: ec787d2 updated the CellsNode field doc to 'ONE OR MORE visual lines' but left the LayoutNode summary a few lines above still saying 'rendered to ONE strip'.
guidance_note: When fixing a stale phrase, grep the file for the phrase itself ('ONE strip') rather than editing only the line the reviewer anchored.

evidence: buildNeededPrefixes now seeds refs from every node's `when`, but the existing gating tests covered only segment templates. The agent added a container-when test. The flag is a false positive: the walkNodes seeding is in the original diff, and adf6330 didn't touch render-payload.
guidance_note: When widening a reachability walk to a new node kind, add a test where that new kind is the only reference to a prefix.

narrative: The diagnostic-path work ran a four-link chain. F2's fix corrected the line but not the path (F3). F3's text-probe discriminator regressed configs with a nested `root` key (F6). F6's structural fix relied on source text the daemon never passed (F7). Separately, F4's doc fix missed a second 'ONE strip' phrase (F8). Round 1 existed only because of F2's incomplete fix.
guidance_observations: Each fix in the F2 chain was tested only through source-bearing helpers; tracing the production call path once would have collapsed three rounds into one.
Partial doc sweeps (fix the anchored line, miss the identical phrase nearby) cost a finding here and in other PRs in this batch.

evidence: `blocks.flatMap((b) => [...(b[i] ?? [])])` copies each row before flatMap flattens it, an avoidable allocation per child row. Returning `b[i] ?? []` gives the same result because the inner array is only read.

The comment called `outline` 'the one remaining unrenderable arm', but DIRECTIONS contains only vertical and horizontal, so outline isn't an arm at all. That also contradicts the same sentence's 'no representable-but-unrenderable direction'.
guidance_note: When a comment describes a union's arms, check each named arm against the actual DIRECTIONS constant.

narrative: This was a small, clean PR. Two minor original findings (a redundant spread and an inaccurate comment) were fixed in one commit, and the second round was clean.

evidence: The rename turned 'one column shape' into 'one shape', while the sibling error says 'one key shape'. 27bd995 restored 'one key shape'.
guidance_note: When doing a mechanical rename, substitute the term one-for-one rather than rephrasing as you go.

evidence: CLAUDE.md:114 still said 'one column shape per key' after a PR whose whole purpose was retiring that term. The flag is a false positive: 27bd995 changed one error string, and the stale doc was missed by the original rename.
guidance_note: When renaming a term, grep the whole repo, docs and CLAUDE.md included, for the old word before opening the PR.

narrative: This was a terminology rename. Round 0 caught a non-uniform substitution, and round 1 caught a doc the original rename never swept. Neither was caused by a fix. Both would have been caught by a repo-wide grep for 'column shape'.
guidance_observations: A rename PR should end with a repo-wide grep for the retired term, docs included.

evidence: Inline onClick emits set-state URLs that need session.id, and inline bg/fg are compiled as templates, but neither was covered by the session.id predicate or checkTemplateRefs. c4029fc added hasInlineOnClick plus ref-checking and frontier seeding. The single-enforcer argument (same color path, so same validation) is substantive; the dataflow citation is decorative.
guidance_note: When adding a new template-bearing or click-emitting surface, list every validator and gate that existing surfaces pass through (ref check, frontier seed, session.id requirement) and wire the new surface into each.

evidence: The original validateClickWrite accepted slash-bearing keys/values and an empty `to`, which the reviewer and agent agree registerStateValidator/makeAllowListValidator reject later. The flag is a false positive: c4029fc did not touch validateClickWrite. verifiable-goals is not the relevant law for surfacing errors earlier.
guidance_note: When a new surface writes into an existing validator registry, mirror the existing sibling's (widget set-action) load-time checks in the first version.

evidence: F2's fix (3005ad7) wrote 'the set-state wire splits on "/" so a slash-bearing key cannot be addressed', but encodeSegments percent-encodes `/` as %2F. The agent had narrowed exactly this claim in cc-candybar#60/F13, so the fact was already established.
guidance_note: When a fix's error message explains why, check the stated mechanism against the codec (encodeSegments) and state the actual enforcer's policy instead.

evidence: This is the same wrong rationale as F3, on the `to` value message added in 3005ad7 ('the set-state wire splits values on "/"'). 50f6b85 restated it as validator-registry policy.
guidance_note: When a fix's error message explains why, check the stated mechanism against the codec (encodeSegments) and state the actual enforcer's policy instead.

evidence: SESSION_ID_VAR = 'session.id' was added in dsl-types although SESSION_ID_VAR_NAME already existed in var-system/sources.ts; 50f6b85 deleted the duplicate. The flag is a false positive: the constant is in the original diff, and 3005ad7 did not touch dsl-types.
guidance_note: Before adding a named constant for a conventional string, grep for that literal ('session.id') to find an existing owner.

narrative: Original gaps in the new inline surface (missing gates, missing load-time checks, a duplicate constant) were fixed across rounds. F2's fix added error messages claiming the wire splits on '/', which contradicts encodeSegments and a fact the agent itself established in #60/F13. That cost two findings in round 2, although round 2 also carried the original F5.
guidance_observations: Rationale text in error messages is code too; the agent should check it against the codec before writing it, especially when an earlier PR already settled the fact.

evidence: The inline leaf returned `[collapseToCell(fragmentsToCells(...))]` unconditionally, so an empty leaf produced one empty strip item. The segment path had a `cells.length === 0 -> []` guard. 704fb10 routed inline through applySegmentLayout.
guidance_note: When adding a second caller of a collapse primitive, route it through the same wrapper that enforces the empty-input invariant instead of calling the primitive directly.

evidence: The helper loops `while ((m = LINK.exec(rendered)) !== null)`, which drains to null, and a failed exec resets lastIndex to 0, so later calls are not affected. The agent conceded this ('the drain-to-null loop happened to self-reset') and rewrote it anyway, and the rewrite's new comment drew F4. The flag is a false positive: d05e838 bumped a package and edited strip-flex.test.ts, while linkUrls is original.
guidance_note: When the reply itself concedes the reported failure can't occur, push back instead of rewriting; the rewrite is new surface for the next round.

evidence: The PR body said ^0.5.0, but d05e838 bumped the dependency to ^0.5.1 and 15ee27b later to ^0.5.2. The drift came from the agent's own unprompted follow-up bumps, not from a fix for a finding, so caused_by is null.
guidance_note: When pushing a follow-up commit that changes something the PR description states (a version), update the description in the same push.

evidence: 15ee27b, F2's fix, kept the dead empty-URL check as `.filter((url) => url.length > 0)` and added the comment 'The close sequence carries an empty URL; keep only the opens', yet the `([^\x1b]+)` capture can never match a close. The dead check predates the fix, but the misleading comment is new.
guidance_note: When rewriting a helper, check each carried-over guard against the regex or type that feeds it before writing a comment that justifies the guard.

evidence: CHEVRON embedded the raw U+E0B0 glyph, while test/strip-flex.test.ts uses the \uE0B0 escape. This is a minor consistency fix. The flag is a false positive: the constant is in the original test file, and 15ee27b changed only linkUrls and the package version.
guidance_note: When writing a private-use glyph in source, use the escape form the neighboring tests already use.

narrative: The rendering-unit change was sound, and F1 caught a real empty-leaf cap bug. F2 claimed a lastIndex bug that the drain-to-null loop prevents; the agent conceded that and rewrote anyway, and the rewrite's new comment drew F4. F3 was description drift from the agent's own dependency bumps. Round 3 also carried the original F5, so no round was purely avoidable.
guidance_observations: Accepting a finding whose premise the reply itself refutes generated the next round's finding; a one-line pushback would have ended the thread.
Unprompted follow-up commits during review (dependency bumps) need the PR description updated in the same push.

evidence: The old block ('vertical container of cells leaves') survived directly above the new accurate comment, so two divergent descriptions sat back to back. The agent deleted the stale one.
guidance_note: When replacing a function's doc comment, delete the old block in the same edit and re-read the region above the function before committing.

evidence: After nodeContributions was removed, deriveValidators and deriveWidgetValidators both reduced to `mergeContributions(widgetContributions(config))`. deriveValidators now delegates.
guidance_note: When deleting one input to a merge function, check whether the function has collapsed into an existing sibling and delegate instead of keeping two bodies.

narrative: A large deletion-heavy refactor drew only two findings, both leftovers of the deletion: a stale doc block and two functions that had become duplicates. Both were fixed in one commit, and the second round was clean.
guidance_observations: After a large deletion, re-read the surviving neighbors of deleted code for stale docs and newly duplicated bodies.
